messages:
oncall-bot: Pager alert: routing-service high error rate on /v1/embeddings (503s). Impact: spike from baseline 0.1% -> 7.8% over last 3m. Possible cause: fallback routing to pinned variant mismatch. Please respond. docs/incidents/protocols for triage steps.

Sophia.eng: I'm on it. Jumping into routing dashboard, pulling recent rollout pins.

Ajay.sre: I see a recent pin anchor change at 3297649000 by darren.ops: alias 'embed-tenant-A' pinned -> "chat-instruct-v3" (was embed-slim-v1). That's almost certainly the problem: embeddings route hitting a chat/instruct variant and returning structured text, not vectors.

Sophia.eng: Wow. That matches error traces — inference proxy log shows content-type mismatch: expected binary tensor, got JSON with "assistant:" fields. Pasting tail of pod logs:

```
2026-03-15T18:32:10Z inference-proxy[req=0x7f] WARN fallback selected variant=chat-instruct-v3 for route=embed-tenant-A
2026-03-15T18:32:11Z inference-proxy ERROR marshalling embedding response: unexpected output shape
2026-03-15T18:32:11Z http 503 /v1/embeddings tenant=tenant-A err=invalid_output_shape
```

Darren.ops: I pushed that pin for a canary to test a new alias mapping earlier this morning — I thought it would only affect dark traffic but apparently the routing policy allowed fallback to pinned variant if primary path fails. My bad.

Emily.pm: Customer impact check: billing notes show two enterprise customers (tenant-A, tenant-B) using embeddings for production search experienced degraded results starting ~18:31 UTC. CS reports: "search results returning paragraphs of text instead of embedding vectors". Potential P0.

Ajay.sre: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Revert pin (rbctl alias unpin embed-tenant-A) 2) Tweak fallback policy to reject incompatible variants (routerctl set fallback.action=reject) 3) Roll new routing rule to prefer model capability filtering. We should do the least blast radius approach first: revert the pin.

Sophia.eng: Agreed. I'll prepare revert patch. Running safe revert command now:

```
# dry-run
rbctl alias inspect embed-tenant-A --show-pin
# revert
rbctl alias unpin embed-tenant-A --actor=darren.ops --reason="rollback mis-pinned canary"
```

Deploy-bot: Revert request queued: rbctl job 77921. ETA ~45s to apply across control-plane.

Ajay.sre: While revert is propagating, set immediate guard to block mismatched interface fallbacks:

```
routerctl patch-policy --alias embed-tenant-A --set "fallback.allowed_interfaces=[embeddings]"
```

Darren.ops: Patch applied to control-plane policy (scope=tenant-A). Confirmed: policy now rejects chat/instruct variants for embeddings route.

Sophia.eng: Revert finished. Control-plane shows alias unpinned at 3297654360. Rolling checker: firing synthetic embedding requests to canary region.

Sophia.eng: Synthetic checks green in us-west-2 and eu-central-1. Error rate falling (503s from 7.8% -> 0.2% in 3m).

Customersupport.bot: Alert sent to CSMs: "Incident affecting embeddings for tenant-A & tenant-B starting 18:31 UTC. Mitigated 18:34 UTC. Engineering investigating root cause and next steps." Template used: INCIDENT-EMBED-504-CSA.

Emily.pm: Good. Can we confirm no persisted bad outputs made it into customers' downstream indexers? CS says tenant-A ran a nightly ingest at 18:00 UTC — but the failures started at 18:31 so there is risk for partial ingestion. @customersupport.bot please flag tenant-A and tenant-B for manual reindex recommendation and create a severity ribbon.

Customersupport.bot: Ticket created: CS-7452 (tenant-A) and CS-7453 (tenant-B) with priority P1 and recommended action "reindex embeddings generated between 18:31-18:36 UTC".

Ajay.sre: Post-mitigation checks: router metrics show no fallback to chat-instruct-v3 for embed routes after policy patch. No 5xx spikes in the last 10m. We'll keep monitoring for 1h.

Sophia.eng: Raising a short-term guard in prod repo to prevent any future alias pins that map embeddings -> non-embedding-capable variants. WIP PR: https://git.internal/routing/PR/512 (adds capability validation at pin time).

Darren.ops: I'm drafting an internal blameless note: "Mistaken pin of chat-instruct-v3 to embed alias led to incompatible fallback causing 503s and customer-impacting bad outputs. Root cause: canary pin allowed fallback semantics and lacked capability validation. Remediation: immediate unpin + policy override + guardrails PR + CS outreach."

Emily.pm: Timeline for postmortem? Let's aim for 72 hours. Need to include: incident summary, timeline, customer impact, root cause, mitigations, and action items with owners. I'll own follow-up and customer comms.

Ajay.sre: Action items (short):
- ajay.sre: Monitor routing metrics and confirm stabilization (1h)
- sophia.eng: Merge PR to enforce capability validation at pin time (ETA 24h)
- darren.ops: Add change-control checklist for pins and require dark traffic flag for experiments (ETA 48h)
- emily.pm: Draft customer-facing note and coordinate reindex offer (ETA 6h)

Sophia.eng: Quick note for postmortem: add example of incompatible outputs and a snippet of matching logs. I'll attach logs to the ticket.

Deploy-bot: Canary checks complete: all good. No regressions detected.

Darren.ops: Sorry team. I'll schedule a retro with the routing owners to make sure pins are gated.

Emily.pm: Closing update for now: incident mitigated, customers notified, postmortem + action items owner-assigned. Will update CS once postmortem draft is ready.

Sophia.eng: Adding final timestamped snapshot to incident ticket. Leaving monitoring on for 60m.

oncall-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated). Duration: ~3m. Follow-up: create postmortem and attach to internal incident tracker IR-2026-03-15-01.
